speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. You've been having a fever and altered mental state for two days; can you tell me if you've had any recent travel, mosquito bites, or head injuries? Also, have you noticed any stiff neck or severe headache?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your current medication, has the fever been accompanied by muscle rigidity, excessive sweating, or changes in your vital signs like an irregular pulse? I also need to know if your family has noticed any worsening of your tics or new involuntary movements.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do you have a history of recent dehydration, and have you experienced any chest pain or shortness of breath? I will now request your vital signs, specifically your current body temperature and heart rate, as well as a CK (creatine kinase) level to check for muscle breakdown.

REQUEST TEST: CK_level
REQUEST TEST: Vital_Signs

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital_Signs: Temperature 39.6°C (103.2°F), Heart_Rate 116/min; Laboratory_Tests: Creatine_Kinase 5600 U/L (elevated).

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of high fever, generalized rigidity, altered mentation, and significantly elevated creatine kinase while taking haloperidol is highly concerning. I need to confirm if you have stopped taking your medication recently or if the dose was increased, and have you noticed any autonomic instability like fluctuating blood pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of tics, currently on a low dose of haloperidol. Social history: Patient details on social and occupational history not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You mentioned a history of tics on a low dose of haloperidol; did anyone recently change your dosage or add any new medications? Your symptoms of high fever, rigidity, sweating, and elevated CK strongly suggest Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, so I will now request a complete blood count and electrolyte panel to assess for complications.

REQUEST TEST: CBC
REQUEST TEST: Electrolytes

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Laboratory_Tests: Complete_Blood_Count: White_Blood_Cell_Count 14,700/mm3 (elevated); Electrolytes: Data not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated white blood cell count further supports the suspicion of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I have gathered enough clinical evidence from your history, symptoms, and lab results to make a determination. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
